verdict.rationale: Kino's own pages describe an in-product agent you can hand work to. It makes cuts from your footage, one-shots each video variant, answers review comments, and can be handed a node, and one hands-on user found it easier to nudge and control than using Claude Code directly. Some docs also describe external agents (Claude Code, Cursor, cloud agents) driving Kino over MCP, so it is not fully clear how native the assistant is. Missing for 10: explicit documentation that the assistant is a native, built-in agent rather than a bridge to external agents, and in-depth docs on what tasks it can and cannot take on.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can delegate tasks to a built-in AI assistant inside the product

citations.quote: Ask for the cut. The agent reads your footage, makes the edit, and leaves every clip on the timeline for you to move.
Manage many variants of your video and ask the agent to one-shot each.
Comments land on your timeline, and the agent can answer them.
hand a node to your agent
